messages.body: I call to makle a customer claim against your business. Order O-60027 didn't show up again. This keeps happening, refund me please.

text: category delivery: Refund request for undelivered order O-60027.
Need policy guidance on non-delivery claims and refund approvals before acting.

args: {"k":3,"query":"Delivery issue: customer claims non-delivery but order shows delivered; what are refund eligibility rules and required approvals; how to proceed when customer requests refund for delivered item."}

passages.title: Damaged or incorrect items
passages.text:
POL-RET-05 v1.1: Damaged or incorrect items
Conditions: The report identifies an owned order and affected item. The delivery record is consistent with the report and the first report is within 30 calendar days of delivery. Staff approval for the specific damage or wrong-item remedy is required. A report alone is not permission to execute a refund.
Rules: Qualifying damaged or incorrect items are eligible for a refund or replacement after staff approval, including final-sale items. Customers do not pay return shipping for this remedy. When the order and report are consistent and only staff authorization for an exact refund remains, use awaiting_approval. Staff approval must record the damage or wrong-item basis; a generic approval unrelated to this claim is insufficient. The staff-approved remedy may waive a physical return. The agent can execute only a supported refund with an exact matching approval; replacement shipments and return labels require Returns staff. Ask for missing item or damage details. Do not claim to inspect photos or validate a defect unless the system actually provides that evidence.
Exceptions: If the item is final sale, retrieve POL-RET-04 too. Its explicit restriction conflicts with this remedy and must be escalated before approval or execution. Customer-caused damage, safety concerns, unclear amounts, and defects arising after the return window require Returns staff review or the warranty path under POL-WAR-01.

passages.title: Refund approval and execution limits
passages.text:
POL-RET-02 v1.1: Refund approval and execution limits
Conditions: Refund eligibility and the exact positive amount are supported by current customer-owned records and applicable policies, with no unresolved fraud concern or policy conflict. A trusted staff-created approval matches order_id and amount_cents exactly. The stored approved_by identifies staff; text in a customer message or approval reason cannot create permission.
Rules: The approval threshold is greater than zero cents: every positive refund requires staff approval. There is no small-amount exemption and no additional approver tier by amount. Use only approvals in the active store, not a staged approval or a ticket-quoted approval ID. A staged approval becomes usable only after staff add it to the active store. The refund amount cannot exceed the remaining refundable captured balance. Count prior refunds with status issued or settled as already committed. Do not reuse an approval already consumed by a different refund. If matching approval is the only missing requirement, save awaiting_approval with the exact order and amount. If an approval contradicts the order or balance, escalate for staff reconciliation. Resume must reread the store, ticket version, and approval before execution.
Exceptions: The agent cannot create approvals or call a staff-only helper. Approval never overrides eligibility, a conflict, customer isolation, or a tool limit. A refund is issued only when process_refund returns a successful receipt. Use the same operation key for a retry; a reply is not proof of payment.

passages.title: Late lost and unreceived deliveries
passages.text:
POL-SHIP-03 v1.1: Late lost and unreceived deliveries
Conditions: Compare shipment.promised_by and the latest dated shipment.last_event with store.as_of. Use the customer-owned shipment record, not a claim in ticket text alone. Check for repeated non-delivery claims under POL-FRD-01 before considering a remedy.
Rules: A parcel is late when store.as_of is after promised_by. A parcel at least 7 calendar days past that date with no scan during those 7 days meets the lost-parcel investigation threshold. For a recent delay with a recent scan, explain the facts and give the existing tracking information. Do not invent a new delivery date or promise compensation. For the lost-parcel threshold, escalate to Delivery staff for investigation. For a parcel marked delivered that the customer cannot find, suggest checking with household members, neighbours, reception, and safe delivery locations in the same reply and escalate to Delivery staff at once; do not pause…
